summary: David J. Kalupahana was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Ceylon and earned his PhD at the University of London under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman, later holding posts at Ceylon and the University of Hawaiʻi.

David John McCutchion specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at Jesus College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at Visva-Bharati University, Jadavpur University, and the University of Sussex.

David Jones is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He held positions at the University System of Georgia and the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell University. He held academic posts at SOAS, the University of Michigan, and Cornell University, and served as president of the Association for Asian Studies.

David Kerman Tomlinson works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold, having also studied with Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman, and held a post at Smith College.

David Kopf was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at the University of Minnesota from approximately 1967 to 1997.

David L. Gosling is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, University of Cambridge, in 1992, with an affiliation at the University of Cambridge attested in 2001.

David L. Haberman is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder. He held posts at the University of Arizona and Indiana University Bloomington, where he became Professor Emeritus.

David L. McMahan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the University of Vermont, and held professorial appointments at Franklin & Marshall College.

David Llewellyn Snellgrove was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge under H. W. Bailey and Walter Simon, and with Giuseppe Tucci. He spent his career at SOAS, University of London, from 1950 to 1982.

David Lopes was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the Curso Superior de Letras and INALCO. He held teaching posts at the Liceu Central, Curso Superior de Letras, and the University of Lisbon.

David Ludden is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He held academic posts at the University of Virginia, the University of Pennsylvania, BRAC University, and New York University.

David M. DiValerio specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan, SIT, and the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, later joining the faculty at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee in 2011.

David M. Knipe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Mircea Eliade. He spent his academic career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, eventually becoming Professor Emeritus.
David Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as President Emeritus at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.
David Max Moerman is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has held academic appointments at Barnard College and Columbia University, serving as department chair.

David Mitchell is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cleveland State University and Ohio State University, and was appointed Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver in 2015.

David N. Lorenzen is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under A. L. Basham, later serving as a long-time professor at El Colegio de México.

David Oliver Allen was an Indologist and historian who studied at Amherst College and Andover Theological Seminary. He served as a missionary for the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions and superintendent at the American Mission Press.

David Ownby is a historian of Sinology and religion who earned his degrees at Vanderbilt and Harvard University. He held academic posts at Southern Methodist University and was a professor of history at Université de Montréal from 1994 to 2023.
